references.text: The one who trusts in their wealth will fall. [ref:Prov 11:28|Proverbs 11:28] warns against placing confidence in riches, which is precisely the danger Jesus points out for those who have many possessions.

In [ref:Luke 18:25|Luke 18:25], Jesus expands on this statement with the image of a camel going through the eye of a needle, emphasizing how difficult it is for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 19:23-24|Matthew 19:23-24] recounts the same scene where Jesus says it is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven, using the camel and the needle's eye as an illustration.
In [ref:Mark 10:23-25|Mark 10:23-25], we find Mark's parallel account where Jesus looks at his disciples and says the same thing about how difficult it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God.

Paul warns in [ref:1 Tim 6:9-10|1 Timothy 6:9-10] that those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a trap, and that the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil – this sheds light on why wealth makes it difficult to enter God's kingdom.
[ref:James 5:1-3|James 5:1-3] speaks sharply to the rich about the judgment awaiting them and highlights the dangers of hoarding wealth, in line with Jesus' warning.

Agur's prayer in [ref:Prov 30:8-9|Proverbs 30:8-9] asks for neither poverty nor riches, because wealth can lead one to deny God – an insight that underlies Jesus' words about the difficulty rich people face entering God's kingdom.
[ref:Ps 62:11|Psalm 62:11] admonishes: "Do not trust in riches when they increase." This is the background for Jesus' warning that wealth can become an obstacle to the kingdom of God.

In the parable of the rich farmer in [ref:Luke 12:15-21|Luke 12:15-21], Jesus warns against greed and shows that accumulating wealth for oneself without being rich toward God leads to destruction – the same theme as in 18:24.
[ref:Luke 6:24|Luke 6:24] pronounces a "woe" upon the rich, because they have already received their comfort. This underscores the same warning about the danger of wealth that Jesus gives in 18:24.
[ref:Heb 13:5|Hebrews 13:5] urges us to keep our lives free from the love of money and be content with what we have, which explains why wealth can hinder entry into God's kingdom.
